sections.h2: Which Clark County offices handle Vancouver property tax?
sections.html:
Clark County handles it, and its Treasurer, Assessor and Board of Equalization all work out of the Public Service Center at 1300 Franklin Street in downtown Vancouver. The Assessor values the property, the Treasurer bills and collects, and the Board hears value appeals.

  • Treasurer: 564.397.2252, treasoff@clark.wa.gov, in the second-floor Joint Lobby. The lobby is open Monday through Thursday from 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and phone and email service runs Monday through Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Assessor: 564.397.2391, assessor@clark.wa.gov.
  • Board of Equalization: Suite 650, 564.397.2337, BOE@clark.wa.gov.

The county's Treasurer page lists the second-half 2026 due date as October 31, with a news release announcing payment on Monday, November 2 because the 31st fell on a Saturday. Neither date is still open.

sections.h2: What is Vancouver, Washington like for a seller?
sections.html:
Vancouver sits on the north bank of the Columbia River directly across from Portland, Oregon, and serves as the Clark County seat. Wikipedia traces it to Fort Vancouver, founded in 1825, with incorporation on January 23, 1857. World War II shipbuilding under Henry Kaiser pushed the population from about 18,000 to more than 80,000 within months, and neighborhoods such as Fruit Valley, Burton Homes and McLoughlin Heights grew from that wave of workers.

The 1997 annexation added 11,258 acres and 58,171 residents, and the city is often thought of as split into West and East Vancouver along NE Andresen Road. More than a third of the urban area's population lives in unincorporated areas just north of the city limits, including Hazel Dell, Felida, Orchards and Salmon Creek. Check your parcel on the county's Property Information Center to see whether it is inside city limits, because the levies differ.

  • Population: 199,698 in July 2025 on 48.74 square miles of land.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 50.8 percent.
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $462,400.
  • Median gross rent: $1,702.
  • Median household income: $81,338.
  • Mean commute: 23.2 minutes, per the Census Bureau's QuickFacts.

sections.h2: What is the property tax rate in Vancouver?
sections.html:
Clark County's 2026 levy report puts the total levy for the tax area covering the City of Vancouver and Vancouver School District 37 (tax area 037000) at $9.6856 per $1,000 of assessed value. Other tax areas inside the city carry different districts, so the rate printed on your own statement is the one that applies.

sections.h2: When is Vancouver property tax due and what if it is late?
sections.html:
The first half or the full year is due April 30, and the second half is due October 31. A payment mailed on the due date counts only if the Postal Service postmarks it that day, and the county's FAQ page recommends handing it to a post office clerk rather than dropping it in a box. Paying by e-check online is free and is another way to pay on the due date itself. Statements for the first half are usually available by March 15, and for the second half by September 15.

Late interest follows state law. For tax years 2023 and later on a residential parcel with four or fewer units, the county charges 0.75 percent per month with no penalty. Other parcels pay 1 percent per month plus penalties of 3 percent on June 1 and 8 percent on December 1.

  • Real property that is three or more years delinquent is subject to foreclosure under chapter 84.64 RCW.
  • Once court proceedings start, all taxes, interest, penalties and foreclosure costs must be paid in full before the auction date.
  • When a certificate of delinquency has been filed, the Treasurer accepts payments only from owners and recorded interests.
  • An income-qualified owner-occupant facing foreclosure can ask for a one-time waiver of interest and penalties under RCW 84.56.020(19).

If you are behind, email taxrequests@clark.wa.gov or call 564.397.2252 before you list the home.

sections.h2: Does your mortgage escrow pay Vancouver property tax?
sections.html:
More than 45 percent of Clark County homeowners pay through escrow, according to the Treasurer's Mortgage and Escrow page. If you are one of them, the county does not mail you a statement, and you remain responsible for confirming payment after each installment is due.

The county says lenders sometimes pay the wrong account number or miss a payment. Check the taxes tab on the Property Information Center after April 30 and October 31. If a delinquency notice arrives, ask the lender which account numbers it paid and request a copy of the cancelled check or disbursement record. The county also warns against paying twice, so confirm with the lender before sending your own payment.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Vancouver property value?
sections.html:
Appeal to the Clark County Board of Equalization within 60 calendar days of the mailing date on your Notice of Value, or by July 1, whichever is later. The county's Board of Equalization page says late appeals cannot be accepted, and it counts 60 days from the notice date rather than two months. You can also file a preemptive appeal from January 1 through July 1 of the assessment year.

The Assessor mails most Notices of Value in June and the rest in September, and only properties whose value changed receive one. The appeal is free. A three-member citizen board hears each case in a 15-minute hearing and mails a written decision within 30 days. The county reports that historically more than half of appeals end favorably for the owner, either after talking with the Assessor or at a hearing.

  • Best evidence: comparable sales or a recent appraisal, repair bids and photographs.
  • Other properties' assessed values are not a persuasive argument.
  • Extra evidence must reach the Board 21 business days before the hearing.
  • A decision can be appealed to the State Board of Tax Appeals.

sections.h2: What relief and closing steps apply to a Vancouver sale?
sections.html:
Clark County's senior exemption has three income tiers. For tax years 2024 through 2026 the top income limit is $62,000, rising for 2027 to 2029 to $85,000 under Senate Bill 6162, according to the county's exemption FAQ. For 2027, applicants must be 61 or older, unable to work because of a disability, or a veteran with a disability rating of 40 percent or higher, and must own the home and live in it at least six months of the year. Applications for 2027 open in February 2027, and current participants are adjusted automatically.

At closing, RCW 84.60.020 attaches the tax lien on January 1 and, absent a contract term, prorates the year by the sale date. Ask your escrow officer to confirm both halves with the Treasurer, and check with the Assessor whether an exemption or deferral will end with the sale.

faqs.q: When is Vancouver, WA property tax due?
faqs.a: April 30 for the first half or full year, and October 31 for the second half. In 2026 October 31 fell on a Saturday, and the Clark County Treasurer announced payment on Monday, November 2. That date has passed.

faqs.q: What interest does Clark County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: For tax years 2023 and later on a residential parcel with four or fewer units, 0.75 percent per month and no penalties. Other parcels pay 1 percent per month plus 3 percent on June 1 and 8 percent on December 1.

faqs.q: How long before Clark County forecloses for unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Three years. Real property with taxes three or more years delinquent is subject to foreclosure under chapter 84.64 RCW. Call the Treasurer at 564.397.2252 or email taxrequests@clark.wa.gov to discuss relief.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Vancouver assessment?
faqs.a: Sixty calendar days from the mailing date on your Notice of Value, or July 1 if later. Late appeals cannot be accepted. Contact the Board of Equalization at 564.397.2337 or BOE@clark.wa.gov.

faqs.q: Is my Vancouver address inside city limits?
faqs.a: Not always. Hazel Dell, Felida, Orchards and Salmon Creek are unincorporated communities north of the city limits. Look up your parcel on the Clark County Property Information Center to see which tax area applies.
